canon.title: Laws of UX: Von Restorff Effect

canon.title: Laws of UX: Flow

canon.title: Laws of UX: Law of Similarity
canon.why: Elements sharing visual properties are perceived as related; use consistent styling for related items.

canon.title: Laws of UX: Mental Model

canon.title: Laws of UX: Selective Attention
canon.why: Users filter information to focus on relevant tasks; highlight important elements and reduce distractions.

canon.title: Laws of UX: Zeigarnik Effect
canon.why: Incomplete tasks are remembered better than completed ones; show progress and incomplete states to maintain engagement.

canon.title: Laws of UX: Aesthetic-Usability Effect
canon.why: Users perceive aesthetically pleasing design as more usable, even when it functions identically to less attractive alternatives.

canon.why: Breaking information into smaller, meaningful chunks reduces cognitive load and improves memory retention.

canon.why: Working memory capacity is limited; design should minimize cognitive demands through simplification and clarity.

canon.title: Laws of UX: Goal-Gradient Effect
